review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner, self-review; not independent approval
review.decision: Place Restore layout within the actual tile header grid instead of a floating overlay
review.notes: New user screenshot shows the restore control covering the session title. Exact source appends it to board with absolute top/left and no title reservation. Keep original maximize/restore geometry, single-max ownership, terminal fit and Escape behavior. Use normal header flow, a narrow icon with accessible name, long-title ellipsis and bounded controls. Synthetic real-handler/CSS fixtures only; no actual terminal/session/input. Reviewed before this new test implementation.

cases.description: Maximized workspace header keeps Restore layout separate from the title and tools
cases.setup: Actual maximizeTile/restoreBoard functions with isolated DOM and board/tile geometry; shipped CSS in a synthetic browser at wide/narrow widths with long mixed-language title and keyboard controls.
cases.action: Maximize a tile, resize, switch to another tile, restore via button and existing Escape path; inspect header order, title/restore/control bounds and original dimensions.
cases.expected: Restore button belongs to tile header and precedes its other children, never floats over the title or terminal. Header grid reserves its column; narrow layout shows a named return icon and leaves title/actions usable. Only one restore control exists. Restoring removes it and restores prior tile dimensions; other tiles and existing terminal-fit/Escape behavior are unchanged. No real user session or service is driven.
